stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = 2 \cos{\left(3 \theta \right)} + 3 \) so that its angle at time t is \( \theta(t) = 2 t \). Using a calculator, find the rate at which the particle's distance from the origin is changing with respect to time at the instant when \( \theta = 0.6 \). Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The distance from the origin is r, and by the chain rule \( \frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\cdot\frac{d\theta}{dt} \), with \( \frac{dr}{d\theta} = - 6 \sin{\left(3 \theta \right)} \).
At \( \theta = 0.6 \), a calculator in radian mode gives \( \frac{dr}{d\theta} \approx -5.843 \).
Since \( \theta(t) = 2 t \), \( \frac{d\theta}{dt} = 2 \). So \( \frac{dr}{dt} \approx -5.843 \cdot 2 \), which is about -11.686.
worked_solution.rule_named: multiply by the rate of the angle

options.derivation: dr/dtheta evaluated with the calculator in degree mode and then multiplied by the rate of the angle
the chain rule product formed with r in place of dr/dtheta, so r times dtheta/dt is reported
the rate of the angle left out of the chain rule product, so dr/dtheta alone is reported
